title: Layerwise quant annealing & cohort calibrator for regression monitoring
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background:
Redwood is seeing intermittent quality regressions when deploying new quantization profiles (int8/int4) generated by AWQ and GPTQ across diverse workloads. Current gating is coarse: global thresholds on overall eval scores that miss cohort-specific regressions (short prompts, instruction-following, domain-specific vocab).

Goal:
Build a layerwise quant annealing and cohort calibrator system that (1) evaluates the per-layer and per-cohort impact of quant profiles (AWQ/GPTQ) using production-like traffic slices, (2) uses an annealing-style search to find safe per-layer bitwidth/scale settings that minimize expected quality loss under latency/cost constraints, and (3) produces automated thresholds/gates wired into Console rollouts and the rollback playbook.

Success criteria (measurable):
- Detect >90% of cohort regressions that lead to >2% delta in semantic-similarity metrics on our production prompt cohorts during canary windows.
- Reduce manual rollback incidents tied to quant changes by 60% in the first quarter after rollout.
- False positive rate for auto-block gating <5% on held-out traffic.

Scope and non-goals:
- Includes AWQ and GPTQ quant profiles at int8 and int4 target bitwidths.
- Focuses on evaluation + gating; model re-training or new quant algorithm improvements are out of scope.

Approach / Design:
1) Cohort calibrator: build a lightweight cohort extraction service that mirrors production routing rules to create representative cohorts (prompt length buckets, route tags, customer cohorts, and domain/topic). Each cohort stores a rolling sample of prompts and references to ground-truth or golden outputs when available.

2) Layerwise impact matrix: for a candidate quant profile, run a focused eval harness that toggles quant settings per layer (full precision fallback for selected layers) to produce a layerwise quality delta heatmap per cohort. Capture metrics: semantic-similarity (BERTScore/SemSim), exact-match for structured outputs, normalized logprob delta, and calibrated perplexity shift. Also capture runtime signals: per-token latency, KV cache hit patterns, and memory / overflow events.

3) Annealing-based threshold search: treat per-layer bitwidth/scale/clipping as a combinatorial space and run a simulated-annealing optimizer that jointly optimizes utility = alpha*quality_loss + beta*cost_increase + gamma*latency_regression. The annealer returns a Pareto frontier of candidate profiles and recommended per-cohort gating thresholds (delta tolerances).

4) Canary + rollout integration: wire the calibrator outputs into the Console rollout service: canary cohorts get the new profile under the derived thresholds; if observed deltas exceed cohort thresholds for a configured window, automatic rollback or degrade to a higher-tier profile occurs. Add manual override hooks for on-call and SEs.

5) Robustness tests and synthetic stress: add synthetic perturbations (token dropout, paraphrase transforms, adversarial prefix swaps) during eval to surface brittle failure modes that simple similarity metrics miss.

Datasets and eval harness:
- Production-sampled cohorts (anonymized) + curated reference sets: instruction-following, multi-turn chat, code-completion, and retrieval-augmented prompts.
- Benchmarks: internal semantic-similarity suite, CodeEval small subset, structured-output exact-match set.
- Runner: extend existing eval harness to support per-layer toggles and parallel AWQ/GPTQ profile application.

Telemetry & observability:
- Metrics: per-cohort quality_delta, per-layer impact_heatmap, per-token latency distribution, quant_overflow_rate, model_compare_delta (AWQ vs GPTQ).
- Dashboards: new Console pages: "Quant Cohort Delta Explorer" and "Layer Impact Heatmap" with drilldowns into prompts and token-level traces.
- Alerts: threshold breach alerts routed to SRE + on-call with auto-created incident templates.

Rollout plan & safety:
- Phase 1: offline runbook and eval harness development + internal validation on 3 open-source models (2 weeks).
- Phase 2: small-scale canary (5% traffic) with manual monitoring for 2 weeks.
- Phase 3: automated gating enabled with conservative thresholds for 1 month; monitor false positives and adjust.
- Phase 4: full rollout and documentation handoff to SEs and support.

Deliverables:
- Calibrator microservice + eval harness changes (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1234)
- Console dashboard and rollout hook changes (Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Layerwise+Quant+Calibrator)
- Runbook and rollback playbook (Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/quant-calibrator-runbook)
- Regression test-suite and synthetic stress generator included in CI.

Open questions / Decisions needed:
- How aggressive should alpha/beta/gamma weighting be by default? Proposed: alpha=0.6, beta=0.25, gamma=0.15 with team-configurable overrides.
- Per-customer SLA exemptions: allow whitelisting customers that accept higher quality risk for cost savings? (Product decision)
- Sampling budget: what fraction of production traffic can be mirrored for cohort calibration without violating costs? Proposed starting point: 0.5% per critical route.

Risks & mitigation:
- Risk: cohort drift leads to overfitting thresholds. Mitigation: sliding-window baselines and periodic re-calibration jobs.
- Risk: annealer runtime too long for larger models. Mitigation: stratify search by most impactful layers (from a prior sensitivity scan) and use cached layer-impact priors.

Acceptance criteria / Done checklist:
- [ ] Calibrator can produce per-cohort heatmaps for AWQ & GPTQ profiles on target models.
- [ ] Annealing optimizer emits candidate profiles and threshold recommendations.
- [ ] Console integration: canary gating honors calibrator thresholds and triggers rollback when violated.
- [ ] Dashboards show per-cohort deltas and token-level traces.
- [ ] Documentation, runbook, and PRs merged.
comments: 2025-01-12 - Aisha Patel: Created ticket and initial design. Linked related ENG-20761 and requested initial resource allocation.
2025-01-15 - Marcus Liu: Scoped the annealing optimizer and suggested starting with a 3-layer sensitivity scan to reduce search space. Assigned to myself for prototype work.

2025-01-21 - Tech Review (Ravi Shah): Suggested adding normalized logprob delta and to capture KV cache hit rate as a signal. Noted potential metric correlation issues between BERTScore and human-perceived regression.
2025-01-28 - PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1234 - initial calibrator + annealer prototype. Requesting review from runtime and eval teams.
2025-01-30 - Design feedback (PM - Elena Marquez): Asked to include customer opt-in for experimental low-bit profiles and to add explicit rollback SLA language in runbook.

2025-02-02 - QA: prototype ran on two models (gpt-like-small, llama-like-med). Observed cohort-specific regression in short-instruction cohort for one AWQ profile; annealer recommended enabling full-precision for 2 transformer layers which brought delta down below threshold.

2025-02-03 - Marcus Liu: Updated description with QA notes and linked dashboards (internal): https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/quant/cohort-delta-explorer. Next: address reviewer comments and refine annealing temperature schedule.
